blocks.text: Continue the two-day crossing of the Drake Passage. The ship crosses the Antarctic Convergence, where cold northbound waters meet warmer subantarctic waters. Marine life and bird species change along the way. You’ll watch from the ship, and wildlife sightings depend on conditions.

The Start of the Antarctic Leg

The Antarctic leg begins as the ship sails past the snow-covered Melchior Islands and through the Schollaert Channel between Brabant and Anvers islands. Snowy peaks, blue-white ice and Antarctic wildlife surround you. The expedition team decides the exact schedule of sailings and landings during this part of the trip.

At Danco Island, you may see gentoo penguins, with Weddell and crabeater seals found nearby. At Neko Harbour, you may take a Zodiac cruise and go ashore for views of glaciers and mountain peaks. At Paradise Bay, a Zodiac outing may offer a chance to see humpback and minke whales. After sailing through the Neumayer Channel, you may visit Port Lockroy on Goudier Island, where a former British research station now houses a museum and post office. Around Jougla Point, you may see gentoo penguins and blue-eyed shags. These are possible stops for days 4–7, with each landing and its timing subject to conditions. If conditions allow, you may snowshoe along the shore to the former skiway near neighbouring Damoy Point. The location and time of the outing are decided on board.
